precepts.text: We glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience. When you read Paul in Hebrews 12, nobody rejoices in tribulation, but he gives you the after effect. When you go through hell, you learn patience; and patience, experience: a lot of us come into this truth with experience in the world but no experience in the truth of God. And experience, hope: and hope maketh not ashamed, because we endure to the end. That tribulation goes back to Ecclesiasticus 2: when thou comest to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.
precepts.point: Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, and her converts with righteousness. And the destruction of the transgressors and of the sinners shall be together: wicked Israel gets the same judgment as Esau. They shall be ashamed of the oaks which ye have desired: the idols. Confounded for the gardens that ye have chosen: the churches. As an oak whose leaf fadeth: your understanding is gone. As a garden that hath no water: no water of understanding. And they shall both burn together, and none shall quench them: God gets rid of what he cannot use.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

precepts.why:
For the dross to be purged away, we have to go through some things. Paul shows it: “And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also.” When you read Paul in Hebrews 12 he tells you nobody rejoices in tribulation, but here he gives you the after effect. Why glory in tribulation? “knowing that tribulation worketh patience.” That tribulation goes back to Ecclesiasticus 2: when you come to serve the Lord, prepare your soul for temptation, the hard times. When you go through hell, you learn patience.

“And patience, experience.” Patience gives you experience. A lot of us come into this truth at 30, 40, 50 with experience in the world, but in the truth of God we have no experience. That is the experience we need.

“and experience, hope: And hope maketh not ashamed.” Experience teaches us hope, and hope makes us not ashamed, because we endure to the end, “because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us.”

So the purging of Isaiah 1:25 is done through tribulation. God turns his hand upon us, and what we go through works patience, experience and hope in us, until the dross and the tin are gone.

precepts.text: Ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ, for he is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us, having abolished in his flesh the enmity, the law of commandments contained in ordinances, to make in himself of twain one new man, and that he might reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross. The both are the two nations, Israel and Judah split in Kings and prophesied in Ezekiel to be one nation under Christ; the audience is the same people as the old covenant, Jews and the northern-kingdom Gentiles in the church at Rome.
precepts.point: And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement, the margin says reconciliation. Reconcile in verse 10 and atonement in verse 11 are the same word: Christ died and brought us back to the Father, which is also called adoption. Christianity starts Romans 5 in the middle where it is confusing; start earlier and it is clear.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.why:
“But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ.” Christ came and died for his people; he was cut off for his people. Romans 5:9 says we are “justified by his blood”, and Ephesians says it is that same blood that brings near those who were far off.

“For he is our peace, who hath made both one”. That is the peace of Romans 5:1, “we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ”. And it shows who is being spoken of. Who is the both? The two nations. When you read the history in the book of Kings, Israel and Judah split apart into two kingdoms, and Ezekiel prophesied that our king would come and die for the nation of Israel and the nation of Judah, so that they would no longer be two nations but one nation under Christ.

He “hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us; Having abolished in his flesh the enmity, even the law of commandments contained in ordinances; for to make in himself of twain one new man, so making peace”. What was two is now one new man, with no more division.

“And that he might reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross”. That is the same word as Romans 5:10, “we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son”. Reconcile means to bring together again, and the both being reconciled are the southern and northern kingdoms. So the audience in Romans is the same people God spoke to in the old covenant: the Jews in the church at Rome, and with them the Gentiles, who are the northern kingdom. Christ, by his death, brought both houses back to the Father as one.

precepts.text: Aaron and his sons offered upon the altar of the burnt offering and the altar of incense, and were appointed for all the work of the place most holy, and to make an atonement for Israel, according to all that Moses had commanded. For Israel, not for everybody.
precepts.point: And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement, the margin says reconciliation. Reconcile in verse 10 and atonement in verse 11 are the same word: Christ died and brought us back to the Father, which is also called adoption. Christianity starts Romans 5 in the middle where it is confusing; start earlier and it is clear.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.why:
Romans 5:11 says “by whom we have now received the atonement”, and the margin gives the word reconciliation. Atonement is Christ’s death, which brings us back to the Father. Reconcile in verse 10 and atonement in verse 11 are the same word; that is also called adoption. Atonement is reparation for a wrong or injury: when Christ died on the cross he died for our wrongs. Break the word down in English and it is at-onement: bringing back together again as one. Who did God come to bring together as one? Israel, the two sticks joined together, both kingdoms.

So who was the atonement ever made for? “But Aaron and his sons offered upon the altar of the burnt offering, and on the altar of incense, and were appointed for all the work of the place most holy, and to make an atonement for Israel, according to all that Moses the servant of God had commanded.” For Israel. Not for everybody.

The theology of the world says atonement is the reconciliation of God and all humankind. But God was never one with all humankind. All nations were never one with Israel, ever. The priesthood of Aaron made atonement for one people, and when Christ made the atonement with his own body, he made it for that same people.

precepts.text: They brought forth the he goats for the sin offering, and the priests killed them, and they made reconciliation with their blood upon the altar, to make an atonement for all Israel, for the king commanded the burnt offering and the sin offering for all Israel. All twelve, because Hezekiah was bringing them back together, with the strangers who showed up for Passover. Reconciliation and atonement were through animals, and Christ's body replaced them; atonement, reconciliation, and justification are three words for the same thing, for the same people, with the same God.
precepts.point: And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement, the margin says reconciliation. Reconcile in verse 10 and atonement in verse 11 are the same word: Christ died and brought us back to the Father, which is also called adoption. Christianity starts Romans 5 in the middle where it is confusing; start earlier and it is clear.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.why:
In the days of Hezekiah, “they brought forth the he goats for the sin offering before the king and the congregation; and they laid their hands upon them: And the priests killed them, and they made reconciliation with their blood upon the altar, to make an atonement for all Israel: for the king commanded that the burnt offering and the sin offering should be made for all Israel.”

All means all twelve, because Hezekiah was trying to bring them back together: all twelve tribes, and the strangers that showed up for the Passover.

Here reconciliation and atonement stand side by side, and they were made through the blood of animals. When Christ died, his body replaced them. That is why Romans 5:9 says “being now justified by his blood”: his blood replaces the animals, the works we no longer receive justification from. And the time came, as Daniel 9 foretold, when the temple was destroyed, the priests scattered abroad and not one stone left standing. With no way left to atone with animals, we had to have faith in Christ; otherwise you condemn yourself, indebted to a law you can no longer keep.

So atonement, reconciliation and justification are three words for the same thing, for the same people, with the same God. Reconciliation is the restoration of a friendly relationship, a reuniting; you cannot reunite with someone you were never joined to. Israel was with God before, rebelled until “he was turned to be their enemy”, and through the death of his Son was brought back again. That is Romans 5:10: “when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son”.

precepts.text: Thou gavest a body unto Adam and breathed into him the breath of life, and unto him only thou gavest thy commandment, which he transgressed, and immediately thou appointedst death in him and in his generations, of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds out of number, and every people despised thy commandments. The flood destroyed them as death was to Adam, nevertheless one thou leftest, Noah, of whom came all righteous men: not Ham's or Japheth's lines but Shem's, the righteous line of Seth, Enoch, and Lamech. When they began again to be more ungodly than the first, thou didst choose Abraham, whom thou lovedst, and unto him only thou shewedst thy will, Judith 5:6-9, who left the idols of his fathers, and madest an everlasting covenant never to forsake his seed; Jacob thou didst choose and put by Esau. At Sinai thou gavest the law unto the seed of Jacob, and yet tookest not away from them a wicked heart: the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed and was overcome, and so be all they that are born of him, so the evil remained; then David built the city, and its inhabitants forsook thee and did even as Adam, having a wicked heart, and thou gavest the city into the hands of thine enemies. The same cycle from Adam to Noah to Abraham to now: the righteous line gets the laws, goes off, is destroyed, and repents; the sons of God are not new, destroyed by water before and by fire next.
precepts.point: Moreover the law entered, that the offence might abound: the law was introduced so sin could be understood and exposed, thou shalt not covet, thou shalt not commit adultery, to guide a naturally sinful people. But where sin abounded, grace did much more abound: keeping the commandments we realize how much we rise, fall, and stumble and how much more grace we need than under Moses, where animals could not atone for everything. That as sin hath reigned unto death, even so might grace reign through righteousness unto eternal life by Jesus Christ our Lord.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.why:
“Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men”. Yes, it passed upon all men; all nations are capable of sinning. The question is who God held accountable. Ezra tells the story. God “gavest a body unto Adam”, breathed into him the breath of life, and “unto him thou gavest commandment to love thy way: which he transgressed, and immediately thou appointedst death in him and in his generations, of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds, out of number. And every people walked after their own will, and did wonderful things before thee, and despised thy commandments.” The evil in Adam passed into all nations; Cain and them were wicked by default.

But out of Adam came a specific line God wanted to keep his laws. The flood came, “Nevertheless one of them thou leftest, namely, Noah with his household, of whom came all righteous men”: not Ham’s or Japheth’s line, but Shem’s, the righteous line of Seth. They multiplied and “began again to be more ungodly than the first”, so God chose Abraham: “Him thou lovedst, and unto him only thou shewedst thy will”. Judith shows Abraham’s people left the gods of their fathers in Chaldea and worshipped the God of heaven. God promised “that thou wouldest never forsake his seed”, and “As for Jacob, thou didst choose him to thee, and put by Esau”. There is always that special line God deals with.

At Sinai he gave “the law unto the seed of Jacob, and diligence unto the generation of Israel. And yet tookest thou not away from them a wicked heart”. “For the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome; and so be all they that are born of him.” The same evil that was in Adam passed on to the righteous line. Then David built the city, and “they that inhabited the city forsook thee, And in all things did even as Adam and all his generations had done: for they also had a wicked heart: And so thou gavest thy city over into the hands of thine enemies.”

It is a repeated cycle from Adam to Noah to Abraham to now: the righteous line gets God’s laws, goes against them, destruction comes, they repent, and out of that line the righteous rise again. The accountability for sin fell on that line. That is what Paul does in Romans 5: he gives the origin story of sin, how it killed off the chosen people, and why Christ had to come and die for that same chosen line.

precepts.text: Whom he did foreknow, knew before, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren; whom he did predestinate, them he also called, the elect of 1 Peter 1:1-2, the strangers scattered in Galatia, elect according to the foreknowledge of God, the chosen generation and holy nation of 1 Peter 2:9; whom he called, them he also justified through the blood of Christ; and whom he justified, them he also glorified, Isaiah 45:25, justified and shall glory. Amos 3:1-3: you only have I known of all the families of the earth, therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities; all nations sin, but God acknowledges only Israel's sins and sent Christ for them, and can two walk together, except they be agreed? Before Adam was made, God knew the nation he would justify and glorify through his Son.

But where sin abounded, grace did much more abound: keeping the commandments we realize how much we rise, fall, and stumble and how much more grace we need than under Moses, where animals could not atone for everything. That as sin hath reigned unto death, even so might grace reign through righteousness unto eternal life by Jesus Christ our Lord.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.why:
“So by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous.” Who are the many? Romans 8 answers: “For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.” Foreknow means knew before. Before Adam was made, God knew the nation he would justify and glorify through his Son.

“Moreover whom he did predestinate, them he also called”. The called are the elect Peter wrote to, the strangers scattered throughout Galatia and the rest, “Elect according to the foreknowledge of God the Father”, “a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation”.

“And whom he called, them he also justified”: justified through the blood of Christ. “And whom he justified, them he also glorified”: as Isaiah says, “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.”

Amos says it plainly: “You only have I known of all the families of the earth: therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities.” All nations sin, but God acknowledges only Israel’s sins and sent Christ for them. “Can two walk together, except they be agreed?” The free gift unto justification of life came upon the people God foreknew.

precepts.text: To the saints which are at Ephesus, the same saints as at Rome; Psalms 50:5, gather my saints together unto me, those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice, which no other nation did. He hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, as Eve was in Adam, we the bride in Christ, that we should be holy and without blame, having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself. The adoption is the reconciliation, atonement, justification, and restoration, according to the good pleasure of his will.
precepts.point: Moreover the law entered, that the offence might abound: the law was introduced so sin could be understood and exposed, thou shalt not covet, thou shalt not commit adultery, to guide a naturally sinful people. But where sin abounded, grace did much more abound: keeping the commandments we realize how much we rise, fall, and stumble and how much more grace we need than under Moses, where animals could not atone for everything. That as sin hath reigned unto death, even so might grace reign through righteousness unto eternal life by Jesus Christ our Lord.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.why:
Paul writes “to the saints which are at Ephesus”, the same saints as at Rome. Who are the saints? “Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.” No other nation made a covenant with God by sacrifice.

“According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world”. As Eve was in Adam, we the bride were in Christ, chosen before the world was founded, “that we should be holy and without blame before him in love”.

“Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will”. The adoption is the reconciliation, the atonement, the justification and the restoration.

So the many made righteous by the obedience of one in Romans 5 are the saints God chose in Christ before the foundation of the world. Adam’s offence brought death on the chosen line, and Christ’s obedience brings them back into the adoption that was always theirs.

precepts.text: Hath God cast away his people? God forbid; for I also am an Israelite, of the tribe of Benjamin. God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew: Amos 3 and Romans 8 again.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.why:
If sin reigned unto death over the chosen line, has God given up on them? Paul answers: “I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.”

“God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew.” Which he foreknew: that is Amos 3 and Romans 8 again. “You only have I known of all the families of the earth”, and “whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate”.

The cycle Ezra described, the righteous line receiving the law, going off, being destroyed and repenting, never ended with God throwing his people away. Every time, out of that line the righteous rose up again.

So where sin abounded, grace did much more abound, and it abounded upon the same people God foreknew. Paul, an Israelite of Benjamin, is himself the proof that God has not cast away his people.

precepts.text: I could wish that myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh, my race, who are Israelites; to whom pertaineth, belongs, the adoption, Ephesians 1:5, and the glory, Isaiah 45:25, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; whose are the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came, who is over all, God blessed for ever. Christ came for Israel.

But where sin abounded, grace did much more abound: keeping the commandments we realize how much we rise, fall, and stumble and how much more grace we need than under Moses, where animals could not atone for everything. That as sin hath reigned unto death, even so might grace reign through righteousness unto eternal life by Jesus Christ our Lord.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.why:
Paul’s heart is for his own: “For I could wish that myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh”. His kinsmen according to the flesh: his race. “Who are Israelites; to whom pertaineth the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises”.

Pertaineth means belongs. The adoption belongs to them, the adoption of Ephesians 1:5. The glory belongs to them: “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.” The covenants, the giving of the law, the service of God, and the promises made to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob all belong to the Israelites.

“Whose are the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came, who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen.”

Christ came for Israel. The free gift that came “upon all men unto justification of life” in Romans 5 is the adoption, the glory and the promises that pertain to the Israelites, the people whose sins God held to account from Adam on and whom he justified by the obedience of one.

precepts.text: We glory in tribulations, knowing that tribulation worketh patience, patience experience, and experience hope, and hope maketh not ashamed.
precepts.point: At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh, the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee, thy tabernacle shall be in peace, and thou shalt not sin: Isaiah 60:21 says thy people shall be all righteous. Thy seed shall be great as the grass, and thou shalt come to thy grave in a full age like a shock of corn in its season: Israel's life will be long, forever.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
Job 5:17: “Behold, happy is the man whom God correcteth: therefore despise not thou the chastening of the Almighty.” We get corrected all the time. We might not be happy while we are going through it, but it says happy is the man whom God corrects. Romans 5 shows why.

“And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience.” There is a purpose behind tribulation: it works patience. “And patience, experience”: patience teaches you experience. “And experience, hope: And hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts.”

That means we understand why God is allowing us to go through tribulation. He is teaching us something. While we are in it we might not understand it, but he is saying, I am trying to teach you a lesson here. That is why we do not despise the chastening of the Almighty.

precepts.text: When we were enemies we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son; much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life, by whom we have now received the atonement.
precepts.point: Christ gave himself an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour, and we are to walk in love and become the same sacrifice for our brothers and sisters. When they put you to death out here, the Lord sees it as a sacrifice on the altar; that is what the altar in Babylon represents.

note.label: A Soul Without Purpose

precepts.why:
Leviticus says what the blood is for: “it is the blood that maketh an atonement for the soul.” Paul shows whose blood: “For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life.” When we were breaking God's law, we became his enemies. Being reconciled now, by Christ's life we are going to be saved.

“And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement.” The blood of Christ is what gave us the atonement, so that we can build upon grace. The blood of Christ is more powerful than the animal sacrifice; it is the most powerful thing in this universe.

Read on in the chapter: “For if by one man’s offence death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ.” By one man's offence death came into the world because of sin, and it reigned from then until today; look at our condition. “For as by one man’s disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous.”

That is the platform we have now. The platform we had under the one man's sin, we got messed up on. But Christ did it right this time, so we can build upon him and do it right because he did it right. It is through mercy we make it to the door, because our righteousness is as filthy rags; so nobody should be boasting of how perfect he is. Christ did not come for the righteous; he came for the sick, so he could heal them. And “in bringing many sons unto glory”, his death brings many sons into glory: a new body and a new mindset. So keep on trying, keep on working, and don't give up.

precepts.text: It became him, for whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory. That glory is a new body and a new mindset, so keep trying, keep working, do not give up over the little things you are going through.
precepts.point: As by one man's disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous. The first platform was broken by Adam; Christ did it right, so we build righteousness on him and reach the door through mercy, since our own righteousness is filthy rags. He did not come for the righteous, so brothers who talk down leadership as if they are already healed can be left alone.

note.label: A Soul Without Purpose

precepts.why:
“For as by one man’s disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous.” By one man’s offence death came into the earth, from Abraham to Moses until today. The first platform we had, Adam messed up. But Christ did it right this time, so we can build righteousness upon him.

Hebrews shows where that obedience is leading: “For it became him, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings.” Christ’s death is going to bring many sons unto glory.

Do you know what that glory is? A new body and a new mindset. So while you are here on this earth, keep on trying. Keep on working. Do not give up and do not give in, no matter what. Keep on fighting. The little things you are going through, you are going to be all right.

The captain of our salvation was made perfect through sufferings, so our sufferings are not the end of the story. It is through mercy that we make it to the door, because our own righteousness is as filthy rags. Christ did not come for the righteous but for the sick, to heal them; the ones who talk down leadership as though they are healed already can be left alone. The rest of us keep building on the one who did it right.

precepts.text: When we were enemies we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, by whom we have now received the atonement.
precepts.point: The letters of Paul were written to Israelites living in those lands and called by their names, Romans and Corinthians, the same way we are called American or Jamaican today; written today they would be the letter to the Jamaicans or the letter to the Puerto Ricans.

note.label: Leviticus 6: The Trespass Offering and the Fire That Shall Never Go Out

precepts.why:
Paul writes that “if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life.” The enemies here are Israel, turned into the Most High’s enemy by rebellion, and through the death of His Son the nation is reconciled, brought back together with its God.

And “we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement.” The atonement the priest made with the ram before the Lord is now received by Christ.

The letters of Paul were written to Israelites living in those lands and called by their names, Romans and Corinthians, the same way we are called American or Jamaican today; written today they would be the letter to the Jamaicans or the letter to the Puerto Ricans.

precepts.text: If when we were enemies we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more being reconciled we shall be saved by his life.
precepts.point: Under the law, atonement required animal sacrifice, but the reconciliation the Most High provides now is through the death of his son. You cannot be reconciled to someone you were never joined to, so the reconciliation is for the house of Israel his people.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 29: Hezekiah Cleanses the House of the Lord

precepts.why:
“For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life.”

Under the law, atonement required animal sacrifice. Hezekiah brought “seven bullocks, and seven rams, and seven lambs, and seven he goats, for a sin offering for the kingdom, and for the sanctuary, and for Judah.” The priests sprinkled the blood upon the altar, “and they made reconciliation with their blood upon the altar, to make an atonement for all Israel”.

But the reconciliation the Most High provides now is through the death of his Son. And you cannot be reconciled to someone you were never joined to, so the reconciliation is for the house of Israel, his people, just as Hezekiah’s offering was made “for all Israel.”

precepts.text: As sin hath reigned unto death, even so might grace reign through righteousness unto eternal life.
precepts.point: Grace covers the thorn you sincerely fight, not the sin you commit wilfully; there is a level of perfection the Most High looks for by generation, and not every man is given the same measure.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“That as sin hath reigned unto death, even so might grace reign through righteousness unto eternal life by Jesus Christ our Lord.”

Grace reigns through righteousness, not apart from it. Sin still reigns unto death, as it did over Ananias; grace is for the man walking in righteousness.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 3 A Message to The 7 Churches

precepts.why: Paul explained that yielding of the right fruit of righteousness. “And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also:” There he goes again: glory in tribulations. We have to learn that thing; I'm still learning it. When hell and high water come my way, oh Lord God, help me. We have to learn this thing. “knowing that tribulation worketh patience;” See that: tribulation works patience. That is what we were just reading in Hebrews 12. “And patience, experience;” Patience brings forth experience. “and experience, hope:” Experience brings forth hope. “And hope maketh not ashamed;” Hope makes us not ashamed. Why? “because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us.” So there is a purpose behind the chastisement of the Lord.

SABBATH MORNING CLASS: If Thou Come to Serve the Lord

points: Glory in tribulation: pressure either breaks you or forges you, and nobody becomes David or one of his mighty men without going through the fire of adversity.

Tribulation works patience, and in your patience you possess your soul: if you keep going through the same thing, there is a lesson in it you have not learned, and God cannot bring you to the next level until you do.

note.label: The Art of War - Rules of Engagement

points: Patience brings experience, and experience is why the bishops, deacons and captains can read a situation and counsel, teach and relate; Captain Yahn's prison ministry is that experience at work.
Experience brings hope, the confidence that this is the truth because you have seen what the Lord can do.

note.label: The Art of War - Rules of Engagement

points: Some of you cannot travel yet because the blessing at that level would destroy you; God keeps you where you can identify the test and grow from it.

note.label: The Art of War - Rules of Engagement

points: And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also. Tribulations are not just, you cannot pay your bills. It is struggling in your faith. It is struggling to make righteous decisions. You have got to be patient with yourself and with others until they can get it right.

Knowing that tribulation worketh patience. So patience is the first thing when you start something new. You never know everything about something new. And you have got to have the patience, considering yourself and dealing with an inexperienced child. It has to be repeated. Too often you hear parents say, I should not have to repeat myself, I told you this, that. Okay, you did. Now let us look at the Bible. How many times did God tell the Israelites, keep the commandments or I will judge you? Keep the commandments or these curses are going to come. Stop participating in idolatry. Do not do this or I am going to send you into slavery. How many times have we heard, keep the commandments and live? If you love me you will keep the commandments. Righteousness is the keeping of the commandments. Walk this way in keeping the commandments. How many times have we as adults heard that and still chose not to do it? So imagine the patience that God has to have with us until we can get it right. It is the same thing in your kids and their habits. It is not going to come natural. It is not going to be two weeks, three weeks. Patience does not have a time limit. And this is on the side of gentle parenting, but that gentle parenting is going to come with some whoopings, some strong language maybe, until we get it right.

note.label: From Broken Men Comes Ungodly Generations

points: And patience, experience. Now that we have the patience in giving the instructions, reiterating those instructions, I noticed with my kids and their learning that I have to give them two to three examples to figure out which one works best for them. And out of the three examples that I give them, they might cling to two or one of them. And that becomes the process of how they learn. But I always have to give them those three. And I understand that in my children because that is how I learn. You cannot just tell me this, this and this, and I get it and go perform it. That is not how I learn. You are going to have to walk me through it two, three times, and I am going to have to see how it is best for me to put my hands on it and do it myself until it becomes second nature.

note.label: From Broken Men Comes Ungodly Generations

points: And experience, hope: and hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us. The Holy Ghost is these words. These instructions is pushing us to be better. That is that Proverbs 10:22, the blessing of the Lord, it adds to you and it does not make you ashamed. It does not take anything away from you. It adds to you. It gives you those experiences, those affirmations that you are looking for, even while you are going through hard things.

note.label: From Broken Men Comes Ungodly Generations

points: And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience. When you go through bad things, it teaches you to wait on the Lord.

And patience, experience. The only way you become strong and learn experience in this truth is through tribulations. If you have not been through anything, you lack experience. You have to go through things.

note.label: Born for Adversity

points: And experience, hope: and hope maketh not ashamed.

note.label: Born for Adversity

points: And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also. It may sound crazy to pray for hard times, but we have to embrace that this mission is not for us to be comfortable; then you can prepare and build your spirit in faith on how to handle hard times. Our people mostly listen and turn to God when things go crazy; when you are low, depressed, and oppressed, you have an outlet, a sanctuary, a home.

Knowing that tribulation worketh patience; and patience, experience; and experience, hope. Thank the Lord for hard times, because they make you pure as gold; that pressure makes the diamond. Like exercise, the tears in your spiritual muscles make you stronger to endure. But the only way to get like that is to hear the word of God: study and prepare your mind for what is to come.

note.label: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

points: And hope maketh not ashamed: I am not ashamed, because my Lord is going to comfort me, and in hard times I have brothers and sisters, family, order, and structure within my household and our nation.

note.label: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

points: Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ. Romans 5:1 continues Romans 4:25 with therefore, as Romans 11 continued Romans 10; the chapters and verses were added later, and it is one long letter. Who is justified in the Old Testament? All the seed of Israel. The peace is Isaiah 53:5, the chastisement of our peace upon him, and by his body, not animals, we have access by faith into this grace.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

points: When we were yet without strength, in due time Christ died for the ungodly; while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. Being now justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath, death, through him: his blood replaces the animals, the works we no longer receive justification from.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

points: For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life, the commandments of God. Isaiah 63:10: they rebelled and vexed his holy Spirit, therefore he was turned to be their enemy, and he fought against them, sending nations to overthrow us. Reconcile means to bring together again; was there ever a time in the Old Testament when all nations were with God? He had one chosen people, so the nations were never with him and cannot be reconciled to him. That word destroys Christianity: you cannot remarry someone you were never married to.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

points: And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement, the margin says reconciliation. Reconcile in verse 10 and atonement in verse 11 are the same word: Christ died and brought us back to the Father, which is also called adoption. Christianity starts Romans 5 in the middle where it is confusing; start earlier and it is clear.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

points: Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin, and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned. Sin and death are synonymous, the wages of sin. Yes, all nations are capable of sinning through Adam; the question is who God held accountable. For until the law sin was in the world, from Adam to Moses, but sin is not imputed, charged, when there is no law: Hebrews 9:22, almost all things are by the law purged with blood, and without shedding of blood is no remission, so sin was only imputed where there was a sacrifice. Hebrews 10:18: where remission of these is, there is no more offering for sin, no more animals once Christ died. Romans 4:15: the law worketh wrath, death, and where no law, no sacrifice, is, there is no transgression.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

points: Nevertheless death reigned from Adam to Moses, even over them that had not sinned after the similitude of Adam's transgression, who is the figure of him that was to come. Adam was a similitude of Christ, but not as the offence: Adam brought the offence and Christ brought the opposite, the free gift. If through the offence of one many be dead, paradise removed and the flood, much more the grace of God by one man, Jesus Christ, hath abounded unto many. They parallel: one brought death upon the chosen nation and one brought life upon it.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

points: The judgment was by one to condemnation, but the free gift is of many offences unto justification: whose offences? Israel's, Romans 4:25, our offences and our justification; my righteous servant shall justify many. Paul is giving the origin story of sin, how it killed off the chosen people who always came back to the commandments, and why Christ had to come and die for that same chosen line. As by the offence of one judgment came upon all men to condemnation, even so by the righteousness of one the free gift came upon all men unto justification of life; as by one man's disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous. Acts 13:38-39: by him all that believe are justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses, since almost all things were purged with blood and Christ's death purges everything.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

points: Moreover the law entered, that the offence might abound: the law was introduced so sin could be understood and exposed, thou shalt not covet, thou shalt not commit adultery, to guide a naturally sinful people. But where sin abounded, grace did much more abound: keeping the commandments we realize how much we rise, fall, and stumble and how much more grace we need than under Moses, where animals could not atone for everything. That as sin hath reigned unto death, even so might grace reign through righteousness unto eternal life by Jesus Christ our Lord.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

points: By one man's offence death reigned, and by the offence of one judgment came upon all men to condemnation; death came for every creature, righteous or not, except the few like Enoch and Elijah taken up. Much more they which receive abundance of grace shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ.

note.label: A Soul Without Purpose

points: As by one man's disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous. The first platform was broken by Adam; Christ did it right, so we build righteousness on him and reach the door through mercy, since our own righteousness is filthy rags. He did not come for the righteous, so brothers who talk down leadership as if they are already healed can be left alone.

note.label: A Soul Without Purpose

points: Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ. So we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ — having faith in Christ and keeping the commandments. That is the key to the kingdom.

note.label: SABBATH MORNING CLASS: If Thou Come to Serve the Lord

points: By whom also we have access by faith into this grace wherein we stand. Why? Because Christ died for us, Christ died for our sins. Because back then, under the law of sacrifice, we were put to death for things that now you can repent from. Back then you were getting put to death. And this is what Paul was trying to get to the people: listen, you want to do the law of sacrifice, you have got to uphold everything that the law of sacrifice is telling you to do. Because a lot of them were not trying to believe on Christ. So, oh, you want to do that? Okay, now you have got to uphold all of the law of sacrifice, the turtledoves and all of this. You have got to do everything that it is saying.
And rejoice in hope of the glory of God.

note.label: SABBATH MORNING CLASS: If Thou Come to Serve the Lord

points: And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also. So we glory in tribulations. We glory when we are going through trials and tribulations, because we know the Most High God is dealing with us. The Most High God has not left us; he is still dealing with us in righteous judgement, and he understands that we are trying to get ourselves together.

Knowing that tribulation worketh patience. So tribulation works patience. This is basically the gist of the class. You going through trials and tribulations is what is going to cause patience, because as you get wiser and in understanding, as you are applying the scriptures, you are going to understand what is going on. You understand why you are going through things: that is something I need to fix, I have got to fix something. So it makes it to where, okay, I am going to be patient, I am going to wait on the Lord. I am going through a little something, but I am going to wait on the Lord. The Most High has got something for me.

And patience, experience. With your patience you gain experience, meaning the experience that you have comes from those tribulations, from how you deal with the things you are going through. When you are going through multiple things over and over again you build that experience, you start understanding more. That is why I said there are levels to this truth. You are going to understand more and more how to deal with the situation you are going through.

note.label: SABBATH MORNING CLASS: If Thou Come to Serve the Lord

points: And experience, hope. With that experience you get that hope: I know the Most High is dealing with me, I know the Most High has got something prepared for me. That is what we have got to keep in mind.

note.label: SABBATH MORNING CLASS: If Thou Come to Serve the Lord

points: And hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us.
